questions.q: What is the heir of a Scottish baron styled?
questions.why: A survey of Scots law of 1936 puts the two in one sentence: the heir of a peer is “Master”, the heir of a baron is “younger of”.

questions.q: How did the style “Much Honoured” begin?
options: As a grant from the Crown
questions.why: “Much honoured” began as a courtesy of address, not as the mark of a rank.

questions.q: The old Scots Act on robes gave the barons and the lords of parliament a mantle of which colour?
questions.why: The Act of 1455 gave the lords of parliament one red mantle, which Lord Lyon Innes of Learney read as the barons’, great and small.

questions.q: What did the Treaty of Union do with the baron’s court?
options: Joined it to the English courts
questions.why: This is the Article that touched the baron: his court was a heritable jurisdiction, and the Treaty preserved it as property.

questions.q: Of old, a baron on trial for a crime had the right to be tried by whom?
questions.why: The old law says it in terms: “ane Earle, be Earles; ane Baron, be Barons”.

questions.q: Which flag has a baron no right to fly?
questions.why: The Saltire is every Scot’s flag. The Lion Rampant is the Sovereign’s, and a baron has no right to fly it.

questions.q: In a baron’s court, who gave judgment?
questions.why: Whoever presided, the baron or his bailie, did not judge.

questions.q: On the Lord Lyon’s Rolls in the Gazette, a baron appears as what?
questions.why: A baron is on such a Roll as the head of a house.

questions.q: The baron’s red cap turned up with white fur is the ancestor of what?
questions.why: The baron’s cap — red, turned up with white fur — is the ancestor of the heraldic “cap of maintenance”.

questions.q: In Scots law, what does a barony do for its holder?
questions.why: Mackenzie: “a Barony, as we call it, do ennoble; for Baronies are establisht only by the Prince’s Erection or Confirmation.”

questions.q: When the small barons were excused from Parliament, what was each sheriffdom asked to send instead?
questions.why: The Act of 1428 does not create the distinction between great barons and small; it assumes it, excusing the small barons and freeholders from attendance and asking each sheriffdom to send commissioners instead.

questions.q: In the records of the House of Commons, which members were called “barons”?
options: Members for the City of London
questions.why: The commission covers every person elected “a Knight, Citizen, Burgess, or Baron of any the five Ports”: the members for the Cinque Ports were called barons.

questions.q: In Waverley, what does Sir Walter Scott call his laird of Tully-Veolan?
questions.why: Sir Walter Scott, Innes concludes, "was quite correct when he characterised his laird of Tully-veolan as 'The Baron of Bradwardine'" (p. 157).

questions.q: How did the official Roll of Baronets settle who was entitled to the title?
options: By a vote of the baronets themselves
By a fee paid to the Crown
By the word of the claimant’s family
questions.why: The Roll settled the question by proof, not argument.

questions.q: In the Kilravock papers, who called the baron “laird”?
options: The Queen and the Privy Council
The baron himself, in his own deeds
questions.why: None of them, in anything he wrote or signed, calls himself laird: that was the word of neighbours, clerks and tradesmen.

questions.q: How may a Scottish baron sign a deed today?
options: By his title, as a peer does
Only with the Lord Lyon’s leave
questions.why: A baron can sign as a peer signs, by his title: “Inverness”, or “Baron of Inverness”.

questions.q: Which barony did Parliament annex to the King’s eldest son for ever?
questions.why: In 1469 Parliament annexed “the barony of Renfrew, with the lands and tenandries of the same” to the King’s eldest son “in perpetuity”. The notice of the letters patent of 2023 that made Prince William Prince of Wales names him “Baron of Renfrew”.

questions.q: What does a souvenir plot of Scottish land confer on its buyer?
options: A place in the Land Register
questions.why: A souvenir plot confers nothing: the Court of the Lord Lyon calls such plots “insufficient to bring anyone within the jurisdiction of the Lord Lyon King of Arms”, and they cannot be entered in the Land Register.

questions.q: Barons and freeholders voted together for the shire. Were the freeholders barons?
questions.why: Freeholders were not Barons and everybody recognised that.

questions.q: In the old records, where is a baron most often given his title, “Baron of X”?
questions.why: A charter or a bond will usually show the name; a royal letter will often show the title.
